segments.text: This is another in the series of lectures given by Swami Isvara Surya Bajee,
that is ashram, on Saturday, June 21st.
This will be a continuation of the English Vakyan and Shiva Sutra, Vimarshani.
Atarayatad Bhandra Prashamo Payaam, Upe Rishranta Satatam, Adisthi.
Now, the author puts forth here, the means by which all these three bondages,
Anumala, Maimala and Karmala vanish, and makes you rest in the desired state of consciousness.
Ujjamo Bhairava, there are two kinds of efforts.
One is pastue effort and the another is active effort.
Here, you are concerned with active effort, not pastue effort.
The active effort is elevating effort.
That effort then flows out in active consciousness.
Makes one's universal consciousness shine in one flight.
That is Bhairava. Ujjamo Bhairava.
That active effort is Bhairava because it leads carry you to the state of Bhairava.
Yoyam Prasarrath Rupaaya, Uymarsimaya Samgadow, Jagity Uchshalana-Aatma
Fara Pratiba, Uvanajan Rupa, Ujjama, Rupa Ujdama, Sai Sarvushakhi-Sama Rasinga.
Ashash, Visubaridad Tam, Sakal Kalpana, Kula, Alam Kalalena Mayata, Bhairava.
that active effort that takes you abruptly in one flight to your consciousness and makes
shine the supreme pratyva, the supreme knowledge of being. That effort is Bhairava because all
energies get diluted in each other and they become one energy sātantrśyakti. All energies are diluted
and digested in one energy and also the whole universe is filled with that sātantriya. And all
different shaded perceptions get an end. Sākāle kālpāna kula alam kavlāna mai atāc. It is why
it is called Bhairava. Because it is Bhairava at maka sasurup abhivakti hēt atāc. It becomes the
means of taking you, carrying you towards the state of Bhairava. And this kind of effort is found
in devotees, in real devotees, sādhākāls, who are always introverted, whose consciousness is always
introverted in awareness of God consciousness. This is the meaning of the sutra. It is said also in
Mahalini vizīvā. Again chit-cintaka-śyāva, guru-na-pradeva-data-jaya-te-ya-sama-desa-sambhava-sav-dīrita.
The penetrative state of trance-sama-desa. The penetrative state of trance is called sama-sama-desa.
penetrative state of trance is that, when once it shines before you, there is no way to escape
from this. You are gone in it. You are diluted in it. This trance has digested you. I mean, you are
individual being. This is sādhava-sama-desa. When one is capable of keeping away all the thoughts,
akin chit-cintaka-śyāva and impressions by the elevating infusion of your master, Guru-na-pradeva-data.
Because he infuses this power in you. I mean, master. Atrehi in this shloka, Guru-na-pradeva-data,
this word Guru-na-pradeva-data is found in this way. It is explained in this way. Svas-māt-gurata-pradeva-data.
Then you are capable yourself, then your master will carry you there. Otherwise not. Otherwise, your master will also be
not successful in carrying you there. It means you must be capable of digesting this kind of awareness
in your mind, in your thought. This is the meaning of this shloka, which is explained by our masters.
In sāchandāti uktam, in sāchandatantra also, this is said, ātmuno bairavamrupaṁ bāva-yēthyāstu
puruṣa tāsi-mantra-prasidanti nithu-yukta-si-sundari. O parvati, the one who contemplates on his own self
as one with bairava, ātmuno bairavamrupaṁ bāva-yētu. To him, all mantras are found successful because
he is always one with that samāvishya, when one with that awareness of consciousness. Bāvanam-hyatra
antar muku ujjantratā padevimarshanam eva. In this shloka of sāchandāti, the word bāvan means antar muku
ujjantratā padevimarshanam eva. Just to meditate on, introverted, active state of elevated consciousness,
and antar muku ujjantratā padevimarshanam. Ujantratā padev, active state of elevated consciousness,
and antar muku means introverted. This is explained in spandā in this shloka.
Ek jantā prasaktaśya yatāśyāt aparodaya unmeśa satvīgaya suyantam upalakśeya. Take one thought. We
contemplate on that one thought. Don't go to any other thought, thoughts. Then other movement that
comes in your thought, that is unmeśa, that is spandā. And that spandā you must realize by your
self. Next, evam jākhidī padev pratiba unmeśa awashtambu pāyikam, bairava samāpatim, agjāna
bhanda prasmāyakahyatum pragarsya, etat prāmarshi prakāśa, pagarsā, vithānāma pī prashandbeda
vāsambavati. So, this is already explained how after taking hold of supreme consciousness,
padev pratiba unmeśa awashtambu. Awashtambu means taking hold of supreme consciousness
in an instant. Jākhidī means in an instant. If it is not held in one instant, it won't be held at all.
You have to hold it in one instant. It is shambavas, way up means. You have to hold it in one
instant. Jākhidī. One attains bairava samāpatim, one attains the establishment in bairava, by
which he destroys all bondages or ignorance. Threefold bondages that we have already explained
agjāna bhanda prasmāyakahyatum, after showing this, after explaining this, etat prāmarshi prakarsya,
vithānāma pī prashandbeda vāsambavati. This vithānā, this external state of
domestic consciousness, is absorbed in non-bredistic consciousness. The tānāma pī prashandbeda
vāsambavati.
